system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
## Buyer review — Project Kestrel

| Issue | Seller’s position | What Buyer should want | Recommendation and one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001: General liability cap** | General Warranty Claims capped at **20% of the AUD 24m price (AUD 4.8m)**. | A materially higher cap, calibrated to diligence and risk; preserve separate, higher regimes for fundamental, tax and specific claims. | **Reject as drafted; negotiate a higher general cap.** A 20% ceiling may leave the Buyer materially under-protected for losses arising from the acquired business. |
| **SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket** | AUD 25,000 de minimis and AUD 250,000 tipping basket, with only the excess recoverable. | A lower de minimis and tipping basket, or a deductible basket only if the price and risk allocation justify it; clarify aggregation and related claims. | **Negotiate down and clarify.** The proposed thresholds can exclude numerous real claims and make the Buyer absorb the first AUD 250,000. |
| **SPA-N-003: General claims time limit** | Notify general Warranty Claims within 18 months after Completion; Seller says limitations apply to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise. | A longer period for general warranties, with longer statutory/tax periods for tax claims and separate periods for fundamental and specific claims; no blanket application. | **Reject the blanket approach and extend the period.** Eighteen months may expire before latent issues are reasonably identifiable, and other claim types need tailored survival periods. |
| **SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties subject to the general cap and time limits. | Separate, substantially higher or uncapped liability and longer survival for capacity, ownership and title; address authority and valid transfer expressly. | **Reject; carve fundamental/title claims out of the general regime.** A 20% cap and 18-month limit are inadequate for the core bargain of acquiring 100% of the shares. |
| **SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out** | No express fraud position in the update; Seller says limitations and exclusive-remedy provisions apply to all Claims. | An express carve-out for fraud and deliberate or fraudulent concealment from caps, thresholds, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance, to the extent legally permissible. | **Require an express carve-out.** Without one, the general limitations language could be argued to restrict remedies for intentional wrongdoing. |
| **SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope** | General disclosure of the data room (DD-002 to DD-012), accounts, statutory registers and public records. | Specific, fair disclosure against the relevant warranty, with sufficient detail for the Buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter; no blanket data-room or public-register disclosure. | **Reject general disclosure as a warranty defence.** The letter itself says the records may be incomplete or preliminary, so blanket disclosure could excuse unknown or inadequately described risks. |
| **SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters known by Buyer or advisers, including matters discoverable in the data room or public records. | Limit any knowledge bar to actual knowledge of named individuals after reasonable inquiry, and exclude constructive or imputed knowledge and disclosure alone. | **Reject as drafted.** “Discoverable” knowledge sweeps broadly and could turn access to a large data room into a waiver of warranty protection. |
| **SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent** | Seller will use reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent. DD-002 shows about AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue (~30%) and no final consent or evidence conditions are satisfied. | A condition precedent requiring final, unconditional written consent and satisfaction or waiver of all conditions before Completion; termination or other protection if not obtained. | **Make satisfactory consent a Completion condition, not merely an endeavours covenant.** Bluefen’s revenue concentration makes an unresolved change-of-control consent a material completion risk. |
| **SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility** | Approximately AUD 3.2m outstanding; Seller proposes release following Completion. DD-003 confirms no repayment or final security discharge is included. | Repayment and full discharge/release of the debt and security at or before Completion, with lender evidence and funds-flow mechanics; no post-Completion unsecured promise. | **Require repayment and release at Completion.** A later release leaves the Buyer exposed to acquired debt and continuing security over Company assets. |
| **SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses** | Seller says the AUD 420,000 DD-005 bonuses are its matter and are not separately itemised in the draft funds flow. Disclosure confirms they are conditional and excludes payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs. | Quantify the full cost including on-costs, determine responsibility, and either have Seller fund/pay it or deduct/withhold it through the Completion accounts or funds flow; address any accrued liability. | **Do not leave this outside the price mechanics.** The known conditional bonuses and unquantified on-costs may otherwise become an undisclosed Company liability borne by Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity** | Existing indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; Seller considers it adequate. DD-004 says transfer depends on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee; DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open, without independent verification, and no receipt or confirmatory assignment. | A specific indemnity and Completion deliverable covering payment of all SOW3 fees and effective transfer/ownership of all Project Materials and related IP, with evidence and protection for resulting loss. | **Expand the indemnity and require verified payment and assignment.** The disclosed records do not establish either cleared payment or transfer of the materials. |
| **SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident** | Seller characterises DD-006 as preliminary and not expected to be material; its disclosure says access, scope and notification requirements remain unknown. | Specific warranties, pre-Completion investigation and remediation/notification obligations as appropriate, and a tailored indemnity for losses, claims, response costs and regulatory exposure attributable to pre-Completion events. | **Treat as an unresolved specific risk, not dismiss it as immaterial.** A potentially exposed file of about 1,240 records remains uninvestigated and the consequences are unknown. |
| **SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals** | Three renewals totalling AUD 330,000 are described as ordinary-course operating costs. DD-008 and DD-011 do not establish whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. | Establish timing, term, termination rights and accrued commitments; obtain any needed consent and reflect unavoidable pre-Completion commitments in the price/Completion accounts or a specific protection. | **Seek detail and do not accept the “ordinary course” label as dispositive.** The disclosed records do not establish the Company’s actual liability or flexibility under the renewals. |
| **SPA-N-014: Category separation** | Seller says limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to all Claims, and its limitation package is accepted. | Expressly separate general warranty claims from fundamental/title, tax, specific indemnity, debt/price adjustment, fraud and other agreed categories, each with appropriate limits and remedies. | **Reject one regime for all Claims.** Different claims have different risk profiles, and the Seller’s blanket formulation could undermine negotiated protections. |
| **SPA-N-015: Title verification** | Seller relies on DD-012 share register showing it holds 100% of issued shares. | Verify the register against the constitution, ASIC records, certificates and any options, liens or other rights; obtain title and authority warranties and clean transfer deliverables. | **Do not treat the register as sufficient verification.** The disclosure identifies the Seller’s source but expressly does not establish the Buyer’s independent verification or rule out competing rights. |
| **SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms** | Seller says tax and IP warranties are settled under the general regime; no distinct terms are provided. | Obtain express tax and IP warranty coverage and appropriate claim periods/caps, plus a specific tax indemnity for pre-Completion tax liabilities and clear treatment of known IP risks. | **Keep these terms open pending full drafting and diligence.** The Seller’s assertion does not supply the protections or tailored limits needed for tax and IP exposures. |

*Negotiation points are subject to review of the complete SPA, schedules and transaction mechanics; the Seller’s “STANDARD” labels do not determine whether a term is acceptable to Buyer.*
=== END ADVICE ===
